The causal mask considered is a binary lower-triangular matrix $M$ (where $M_{ij} = 1$ for $j \le i$ and $0$ otherwise). This mask ($M$) is applied as an element-wise multiplication ($\odot$) after the softmax operation on Attention Matrix ($A$).

$$\text{softmax}(A) \odot M$$

Identify the correct statements from the following:

options.label: A
options.text: The approach violates the autoregressive property

options.label: B
options.text:
The approach ensures autoregressive property is not violated by ensuring that 
the final attention weights of future tokens are 0

options.label: C
options.text:
The final attention weights in the new approach will be greater than or equal 
to that of the original approach

options.label: D
options.text:
The attention weights for the final token of the sequence will always be the 
same for both the approaches

questions.stem_text: Which of the following options correctly reflect the internal state updates performed during a Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) training iteration?

options.label: A
options.text:
After a pair is chosen for merging, it is permanently added to the active 
vocabulary list.

options.label: B
options.text:
The algorithm recalculates the log probability of the entire corpus before the 
next iteration.

options.label: C
options.text:
The independent frequencies of the two constituent tokens that were part of 
the merge are reduced by the frequency of the merged token.

options.label: D
options.text:
The original constituent tokens of the merged pair are removed from the 
vocabulary to optimize dictionary size.

questions.stem_text: A baseline T5 model with denoising objective on a span of corrupted tokens is used for unsupervised pre-training. Consider the phrase "life is like a box of chocolates". If the word "life" and the span "box of chocolates" are selected for corruption, which of the following statements correctly describe the training process?

options.label: A
options.text:
The input sequence replaces the corrupted spans with unique sentinal tokens 
as: "<X> is like a <Y>".

options.label: B
options.text:
The output sequence generated takes the form "<X> life <Y> box of chocolates 
<Z>", with the final sentinal token to indicate sequence completion.

options.label: C
options.text:
The loss is calculated exclusively over the generated sentinal tokens and the 
missing text.

options.label: D
options.text:
The decoder reconstructs the entire original sequence autoregressively to 
compute the total loss over all positions.

questions.stem_text: During the fine-tuning of GPT-1 for Textual Entailment tasks, what is the purpose of the delimiter token ($)?

options.label: A
options.text: To trigger the softmax function.

options.label: B
options.text: To separate premise and hypothesis.

options.label: C
options.text: To mark the end of the sentence.

options.label: D
options.text: To initialize the linear head.

questions.stem_text: During the fine-tuning of a decoder-only Transformer for sequence classification, why is the hidden representation of the final input token used as the input to the classification layer?

options.label: A
options.text:
The first token's representation relies exclusively on absolute positional 
encodings and lacks semantic context for classification.

options.label: B
options.text:
The final token's representation is computed independently of self-attention, 
making its gradients more stable during the fine-tuning process.

options.label: C
options.text:
Selecting the final token aligns with the autoregressive objective, eliminating 
the need for teacher forcing during the classification forward pass.

options.label: D
options.text: Causal self-attention ensures that only the final token's representation aggregates information from all preceding tokens in the sequence.

questions.stem_text: In the decoding phase of a Language model, temperature scaling with $T = 5$ is applied to the output logits before performing top-$p$ (nucleus) sampling. Which of the following options best describes the impact of the temperature scaling on the subsequent sampling step?

options.label: A
options.text:
Increases the required number of candidate tokens thus expanding the 
nucleus.

options.label: B
options.text:
Decreases the required number of candidate tokens thus shrinking the 
nucleus.

options.label: C
options.text: Truncates the tail of the distribution causing the sampling to behave similar to top-$k$ sampling.

options.label: D
options.text:
Size of the nucleus remains unaffected by the temperature scaling as it only 
depends on order of the tokens.

questions.stem_text: In the WordPiece tokenization algorithm, how does the scoring formula prioritize token merges?

options.label: A
options.text:
It evaluates the log-probability of the pair and selects the highest scoring 
transition.

options.label: B
options.text: It merges the pair with the highest absolute frequency in the corpus.

options.label: C
options.text:
It prioritizes pairs that occur together frequently but rarely appear 
independently in the corpus.

options.label: D
options.text: None of these

questions.stem_text: Consider the T5 "text-to-text" paradigm. How does the model process fundamentally different tasks such as Semantic Similarity (continuous regression) and Sentiment Analysis (discrete classification) during the fine-tuning phase?

options.label: A
options.text:
The model uses the encoder to output the regression score and decoder for 
the classification tokens switching based on the input prompt.

options.label: B
options.text:
The decoder part of the model is appended with separate prediction heads for 
regression and classification which are updated based on Mean Squared Error and Cross-Entropy 
respectively.

options.label: C
options.text:
The model treats both tasks as sequence generation objectives with task-
specific prefix added in the input and all output is generated as strings.

options.label: D
options.text: None of these.

questions.stem_text: In the context of the BART (Bidirectional AutoRegressive Transformer) architecture, how does the model handle corrupted input sequences compared to its output?

options.label: A
options.text:
The decoder ignores the encoder output and performs standard causal 
language modeling.

options.label: B
options.text:
The encoder processes the original sequence and the decoder predicts the 
corrupted tokens.

options.label: C
options.text:
The encoder processes the corrupted sequence and the decoder predicts the 
entire original sequence.

options.label: D
options.text:
Both the encoder and decoder process the corrupted sequence to calculate 
masked loss.

questions.stem_text: When comparing the C4 dataset to an 'Unfiltered-C4' dataset that is 8 times larger, what was the observed effect on downstream task performance?

options.label: A
options.text: Performance remained identical, suggesting a saturation point in data utility.

options.label: B
options.text: Performance improved only for high-resource tasks like translation.

options.label: C
options.text: Performance improved significantly due to the increased diversity of data.

options.label: D
options.text: Performance degraded across all tasks despite the larger scale.

questions.stem_text: Which of the following describes the 'Adapter Layers' fine-tuning strategy?

options.label: A
options.text: Randomly freezing 50% of the attention heads in each layer during training.

options.label: B
options.text:
Adding small dense-ReLU-dense blocks after FFN layers and updating only 
those and Layer Norm parameters.

options.label: C
options.text: Updating all parameters in the model but using a much smaller learning rate.

options.label: D
options.text: Increasing the dimension $d_{\text{model}}$ of the existing Feed-Forward networks.

questions.stem_text: Which of the following is a reported negative effect of including significantly duplicated content in LLM training data?

options.label: A
options.text: It decreases the model's overall inference speed during deployment.

options.label: B
options.text: It causes the model to generate repeated sequences much more frequently.

options.label: C
options.text: It permanently reduces the maximum supported context window length.

options.label: D
options.text: It causes the model to lose the ability to process multilingual input.

questions.stem_text: If you have a fixed compute budget ($C$) and choose to train an extraordinarily large model (massive $N$) on a relatively small dataset (small $D$), what is the likely outcome according to scaling laws?

options.label: A
options.text: The model will be over-trained and memorize the dataset.

options.label: B
options.text:
The model will be under-trained and less capable than a smaller model trained 
on more data with the same compute budget.

options.label: C
options.text: The model will perfectly memorize the small dataset and generalize flawlessly.

options.label: D
options.text: The model's inference speed will increase dramatically.
